animals.name: phylum: Porifera
animals.traits: porifera (sponges): no true tissues or organs, no body symmetry, body full of small pores (ostia) + one or more large openings (osculum), sessile (attached to a substrate), filter feeders, skeleton of spicules or spongin

animals.name: class: Hydrozoa
animals.traits:
cnidaria: radial symmetry, tentacles with stinging cells (cnidocytes), one opening (mouth) to the gut
hydrozoa: two stages
- polyp (sessile): small, often in branched colonies, ring of tentacles around the mouth (Hydra = single freshwater polyp)
- medusa (free-swimming): small jellyfish with a velum (shelf of tissue under the bell rim)

animals.name: class: Turbellaria
animals.traits:
platyhelminthes: flat body, bilateral symmetry, gut with only one opening (no anus)
turbellaria (free-living flatworms, planarians): body covered in cilia (glide), mouth with a pharynx in the middle of the underside (the light spot), planarians: three-branched gut, 2 eyespots, triangular head

animals.name: class: Trematoda
animals.traits:
platyhelminthes: flat body, bilateral symmetry, gut with only one opening (no anus)
trematoda (flukes): parasites, leaf-like shape, two suckers: oral + ventral, no hooks, life cycle with a snail as intermediate host

animals.name: class: Monogenea
animals.traits:
platyhelminthes: flat body, bilateral symmetry, gut with only one opening (no anus)
monogenea: ectoparasites mostly on fish gills and skin, small (mostly under 2 cm), attachment organ at the back = opisthaptor (suckers + hooks), only one host

animals.name: class: Cestoda
animals.traits:
platyhelminthes: flat body, bilateral symmetry
cestoda (tapeworms): gut parasites, long ribbon-like body of segments (proglottids), up to 20+ m, head (scolex) with suckers and often hooks, no gut

animals.name: phylum: Syndermata
animals.traits:
syndermata
rotifers: microscopic (about 0.1-1 mm), crown of cilia on the head (corona, looks like spinning wheels), chewing jaws (mastax) visible inside, foot with 2 toes
acanthocephala (thorny-headed worms): gut parasites with a hooked proboscis

animals.name: subclass: Caenogastropoda
animals.traits:
gastropoda: one muscular foot, one spiral shell (or none), head with tentacles
caenogastropoda: shell usually closed by a lid (operculum), gills, one pair of tentacles with eyes at their base, mostly marine (also freshwater, e.g. Viviparus), shell often with a narrow opening or a siphonal canal

animals.name: order: Basommatophora
animals.traits:
gastropoda: one muscular foot, one spiral shell (or none), head with tentacles
basommatophora (freshwater snails): one pair of tentacles with eyes at their BASE, no operculum, breathe air at the surface, shell either flat-coiled (ramshorn snails) or tall and pointed (pond snails)

animals.name: order: Stylommatophora
animals.traits:
gastropoda: one muscular foot, one spiral shell (or none), head with tentacles
stylommatophora (land snails and slugs): 2 pairs of tentacles, eyes on the TIPS of the longer pair, no operculum, shell sometimes reduced or missing (slugs), shell can be hairy or with teeth in the opening

animals.name: class: Bivalvia
animals.traits:
mollusca: soft body, muscular foot, mantle
bivalvia (mussels, clams): TWO shell valves joined by a hinge, no head, wedge-shaped foot, filter feeders, live buried in sediment or attached to a substrate (byssus threads)

animals.name: class: Polychaeta
animals.traits:
annelida: ringed worms, segmented body
polychaeta (poly = many, chaite = bristles): mostly marine, pair of parapodia on every segment with many bristles, head with antennae, palps and tentacles

animals.name: class: Oligochaeta
animals.traits:
annelida: ringed worms, segmented body
oligochaeta (oligos = few, chaite = bristles; earthworms): no parapodia, only 4 pairs of short bristles on each segment, clitellum (saddle) in adults, head with no appendages, in soil and fresh water

animals.name: class: Hirudinea
animals.traits:
annelida: ringed worms, segmented body
hirudinea (leeches): 34 segments (each with several outer rings), 2 suckers (front + back), 1-5 pairs of eyes, no bristles, flattened body

animals.name: phylum: Nematoda
animals.traits: nematoda (roundworms): smooth, not segmented, round in cross-section, tapered at both ends, often a pointed tail, males often with a curled tail

animals.name: order: Anostraca
animals.traits:
ano = without, straca = shell
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leaf-like limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
anostraca (fairy shrimps, brine shrimps): no carapace (shell), 11 pairs of leaf-like limbs, 2 compound eyes on stalks + a 3rd (naupliar) eye in the middle, males with large clasping antennae, swim on their back

animals.name: order: Notostraca
animals.traits:
noton = back
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leaf-like limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
notostraca (tadpole shrimps, Triops): large flat shield (carapace) covering the head and thorax, 2 compound eyes close together on top of the shield (not stalked), many pairs of leaf-like limbs, long segmented abdomen with 2 long tail filaments

animals.name: order: Cladocera
animals.traits:
cladon = branch, ceros = horn
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. branchiopoda: leaf-like limbs with gills, abdomen WITHOUT legs
cladocera (water fleas, Daphnia): large branched 2nd antennae for swimming, body in a folded carapace, flattened from the sides, one large compound eye, often a tail spine

animals.name: subclass: Branchiura
animals.traits:
branchion = gill, oura = tail
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 thorax segments, no limbs on the abdomen
branchiura (fish lice, Argulus): flat oval shield, 2 large suckers + a sting (stylet), 4 pairs of swimming legs, unsegmented abdomen, 2 compound eyes on top, 5-25 mm, parasites on fish

animals.name: subclass: Pentastomida
animals.traits:
penta = 5, stoma = mouth
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 thorax segments, no limbs on the abdomen
pentastomida (tongue worms): parasites in the airways of vertebrates, 2-13 cm, worm-like ringed body, 4 hooks + mouth on the head (looks like 5 mouths)

animals.name: subclass: Copepoda
animals.traits:
cope = oar
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. maxillopoda: max 6 thorax segments, no limbs on the abdomen
copepoda: about 1-2 mm, 1st antennae very long, one naupliar eye in the middle, large head shield, forked tail, females often with egg sacs

animals.name: order: Decapoda
animals.traits:
deca = 10
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malacostraca: hard (calcified) shell, legs also on the abdomen
decapoda (crayfish, crabs, shrimps): 5 pairs of walking legs (10 legs), 1st pair often with pincers, head and thorax fused under one carapace, eyes on stalks

animals.name: order: Isopoda
animals.traits:
iso = equal
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malacostraca: hard (calcified) shell, legs also on the abdomen
isopoda (woodlice, water slaters): flattened from top to bottom, no carapace, 7 pairs of similar walking legs, short abdomen, compound eyes NOT stalked

animals.name: order: Amphipoda
animals.traits:
amphi = both kinds
crustacea: 2 pairs of antennae, body = head + thorax + abdomen or cephalothorax + abdomen, segmented body and limbs
cl. malacostraca: hard (calcified) shell, legs also on the abdomen
amphipoda (scuds, sand hoppers): flattened from the sides, curved (shrimp-like) body, no carapace, front legs with small grasping claws, eyes not stalked

animals.name: class: Xiphosura
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
xiphosura (horseshoe crabs): large horseshoe-shaped prosoma shield, opisthosoma shield with spines, long spike-like tail (telson), book gills, marine

animals.name: order: Scorpionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
scorpionida (scorpions): small 3-segmented chelicerae, large pincers on the pedipalps, opisthosoma in two parts: broad front part + narrow movable tail, ending in a telson with a venom gland and sting

animals.name: order: Pseudoscorpionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
pseudoscorpionida (pseudoscorpions): tiny (a few mm), 2-segmented chelicerae, large pincer pedipalps with venom glands, no tail, no sting

animals.name: order: Acari
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
acari (mites and ticks): prosoma and opisthosoma fused into one body, mouthparts on a small front part (gnathosoma), mites mostly under 1 mm, ticks bigger, larvae have only 3 pairs of legs

animals.name: order: Opilionida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
opilionida (harvestmen, daddy longlegs): prosoma broadly joined to the segmented opisthosoma = one oval body, very long thin legs, 1 pair of eyes on a bump in the middle, no silk, no venom

animals.name: order: Araneida
animals.traits:
chelicerata: no antennae, body = prosoma (head + thorax) + opisthosoma (abdomen), 1 pair of chelicerae, 1 pair of pedipalps, 4 pairs of walking legs
araneida (spiders): usually 8 eyes, prosoma joined to the unsegmented opisthosoma by a thin waist (pedicel), chelicerae with venom fangs, spinnerets at the end of the abdomen, males with swollen pedipalp tips

animals.name: class: Chilopoda
animals.traits:
myriapoda: head + trunk (14-177 segments), at least 9 pairs of limbs
chilopoda (centipedes): long antennae, 1 pair of legs on each trunk segment, legs on the sides of the body, last pair of legs prolonged, limbs on the 1st trunk segment = maxillipeds with venom glands, fast runners, mostly predatory

animals.name: class: Diplopoda
animals.traits:
myriapoda: head + trunk (14-177 segments), at least 9 pairs of limbs
diplopoda (millipedes): short antennae, legs under the body, 1st segment no legs, 2nd-4th segments 1 pair, the remaining segments (diplosomites) 2 pairs of legs, maxillae fused into a gnathochilarium, slow, mostly detritivorous, can roll up (volvation)
pill millipede (Glomeris) x pill bug (Isopoda): count the leg pairs per segment

animals.name: class: Collembola
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
collembola (springtails): minute to 9 mm, entognathous (mouthparts hidden inside the head capsule), 1st segment with a ventral tube (collophore), 3rd-4th segment with a jumping fork (furca), ocelli or blind

animals.name: subclass: Archaeognatha
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
archaeognatha (jumping bristletails): mandible with a single joint, large compound eyes that touch each other + ocelli, long maxillary palps, up to 15 mm, covered in scales, styli on the abdomen, 1 epiproct (caudal filament) + 1 pair of cerci all pointing the same way, nocturnal, on rocks, jumpers

animals.name: order: Zygentoma
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
zygentoma (silverfish): wingless (never had wings), up to 10 mm, covered in scales, one colour, compound eyes apart or missing, styli only on the last 2 abdominal segments, epiproct + 1 pair of cerci pointing to the sides, much smaller maxillary palps, do not jump, omnivorous, pests

animals.name: order: Ephemeroptera
animals.traits:
pterygota: 2 pairs of wings; paleoptera: wings not folded on the abdomen
ephemeroptera (mayflies): short antennae, 2 long cerci (sometimes + 1 terminal filament), wings held upright, adult does not feed and lives hours to a few days, subimago = cloudy wings + fuzzy body
nymphs: in water, tracheal gills on the abdomen, 3 caudal filaments

animals.name: suborder: Zygoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
odonata: predators, short antennae, ocelli, wings with pterostigma (+ nodus)
zygoptera (damselflies): eyes apart, wings with stems, folded along the abdomen (not touching), slim

animals.name: suborder: Anisoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
odonata: predators, short antennae, ocelli, wings with pterostigma (+ nodus)
anisoptera (dragonflies): eyes touching or very close, hind wings broader at the base than the front wings, wings held flat open at rest, robust abdomen

animals.name: order: Plecoptera
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen, usually a large anal lobe on the wings
plecoptera (stoneflies): cloudy wings folded over each other horizontally, 2 long cerci, long antennae, ocelli, good runners
nymphs: 2 cerci (x Ephemeroptera), gills near the legs, abdomen, mouth

animals.name: order: Blattodea
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen
blattodea (cockroaches): winged or wingless, leathery front wings = tegmens, multisegmented cerci, large pronotum, massive coxae, thorny tibiae, eggs in an ootheca, usually night-active

animals.name: order: Mantodea
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen
mantodea (mantises): tegmens, ootheca, triangular mobile head, raptorial forelegs, prolonged prothorax, short segmented cerci, females often with shorter wings than males

animals.name: suborder: Ensifera
animals.traits:
orthoptera: jumping hind legs, tegmens, 1-segmented cerci, stridulatory and hearing organs
ensifera (crickets and half of the grasshoppers): long antennae, long sword-like ovipositor, hearing organ on the front tibiae, stridulate by rubbing the front wings together, often predatory

animals.name: suborder: Caelifera
animals.traits:
orthoptera: jumping hind legs, tegmens, 1-segmented cerci, stridulatory and hearing organs
caelifera (grasshoppers, locusts): short antennae, short ovipositor, hearing (tympanal) organ on the 1st abdominal segment, stridulate by rubbing the hind femur against a wing vein, phytophagous

animals.name: order: Dermaptera
animals.traits:
neoptera (polyneoptera): chewing mouthparts, wings folded on the abdomen
dermaptera (earwigs): short tegmens, hind wings folded under them (often fly), no ocelli, massive forceps-like 1-segmented cerci (hunting, defence, folding the wings), nocturnal, parental care

animals.name: suborder: Anoplura
animals.traits:
paraneoptera: mouthparts modified into a sucking proboscis, liquid food, reduced cerci and ovipositor
anoplura (sucking lice): wingless, no cerci, usually 5-segmented antennae, fused thorax segments, grasping legs (claws), eyes reduced or missing, proboscis with teeth (haustellum), only on mammals, spread diseases (typhus, trench fever)

animals.name: superfamily: Aphidoidea
animals.traits:
hemiptera: piercing-sucking rostrum, tegmens or hemelytra, extraoral digestion
sternorrhyncha: rostrum base on the thorax between the front legs, small, phytophagous pests
aphidoidea (aphids): long antennae, pair of siphunculi (tubes) on the abdomen, cauda (tail), honeydew, wings membranous if present

animals.name: superfamily: Coccoidea
animals.traits:
hemiptera: piercing-sucking rostrum, tegmens or hemelytra, extraoral digestion
sternorrhyncha: rostrum base on the thorax between the front legs, small, phytophagous pests
coccoidea (scale insects): strong sexual dimorphism; females wingless, sessile, reduced legs, covered by a waxy shield or ovisac (wax glands); males minute, one pair of wings, live a few days

animals.name: suborder: Auchenorrhyncha
animals.traits:
hemiptera: piercing-sucking rostrum, tegmens or hemelytra, extraoral digestion
auchenorrhyncha (cicadas, leafhoppers, planthoppers): rostrum starts at the back of the head, very short antennae (bristle), wings held roof-like, large pronotum, bulging eyes, thick hind legs (jumpers, thorny tibiae in leafhoppers), cicadas sing with a tymbal organ, phytophagous

animals.name: suborder: Heteroptera
animals.traits:
hemiptera: piercing-sucking rostrum, tegmens or hemelytra, extraoral digestion
heteroptera (true bugs): prognathous head, rostrum starts at the front of the head, front wings = hemelytra (leathery base + membranous tip), large triangular scutellum, 4-5-segmented antennae, stink (repellent) glands, on land and in water

animals.name: order: Neuroptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
neuroptera (lacewings, antlions): 2 pairs of similar wings held roof-like, dense net-like venation (forked veins at the wing edge), chewing mouthparts, long many-segmented antennae (clubbed in antlions), usually no ocelli, predatory
larva: long sucking mandibles (antlion pits)

animals.name: order: Megaloptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
megaloptera (alderflies, dobsonflies): smoky wings held roof-like, coarse venation, large head, live near water
larva: aquatic predator with lateral tracheal gills on the abdomen

animals.name: order: Raphidioptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
raphidioptera (snakeflies): very long neck-like prothorax, clear wings held roof-like with a pterostigma, female with a long needle-like ovipositor, predatory

animals.name: suborder: Adephaga
animals.traits:
coleoptera (beetles): front wings hardened into elytra, chewing mouthparts, complete metamorphosis
adephaga (ground beetles, tiger beetles, diving beetles): hind coxae divide the 1st visible abdominal segment, always simple (thread-like) antennae, adults and larvae usually predatory

animals.name: suborder: Polyphaga
animals.traits:
coleoptera (beetles): front wings hardened into elytra, chewing mouthparts, complete metamorphosis
polyphaga (most beetles: ladybirds, scarabs, weevils, longhorns): hind coxae do not divide the 1st abdominal segment, antennae often modified (clubbed, lamellate, elbowed, saw-like), all kinds of food

animals.name: order: Mecoptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
mecoptera (scorpionflies): head prolonged into a beak with chewing mouthparts at the tip, 2 pairs of similar (often spotted) wings, long thread-like antennae, male's genital capsule curled up like a scorpion's tail

animals.name: suborder: Nematocera
animals.traits:
diptera (flies): only 1 pair of wings, hind wings turned into halteres, sucking or piercing mouthparts, legless larvae
nematocera (mosquitoes, crane flies, midges, black flies): long thin antennae with many (more than 6) similar segments, usually slender with long legs

animals.name: suborder: Brachycera
animals.traits:
diptera (flies): only 1 pair of wings, hind wings turned into halteres, sucking or piercing mouthparts, legless larvae
brachycera (house flies, horse flies, hoverflies, bee flies): short antennae with 3 segments, often with a bristle (arista), stout body

animals.name: order: Siphonaptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
siphonaptera (fleas): wingless, flattened from side to side, piercing-sucking mouthparts, no compound eyes, short antennae in grooves, combs of spines (ctenidia), long jumping hind legs, blood-sucking on mammals and birds

animals.name: order: Trichoptera
animals.traits:
holometabola: complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
trichoptera (caddisflies): moth-like, 2 pairs of hairy wings (hairs, not scales) held roof-like, very long thread-like antennae, long legs and palps, no proboscis
larva: aquatic, often builds a portable case of sand, stones or plants

animals.name: order: Lepidoptera
animals.traits:
hexapoda: head + thorax (3 segments) + abdomen, 6 legs (1 pair on each thorax segment)
lepidoptera (moths and butterflies): 2 pairs of wings with scales, proboscis, long legs
larva = caterpillar: legs + prolegs, mandibles

animals.name: suborder: Symphyta
animals.traits:
hymenoptera: 2 pairs of membranous wings hooked together, reduced venation, chewing or lapping mouthparts
symphyta (sawflies, horntails): no wasp waist (abdomen broadly joined to the thorax), no sting (saw-like ovipositor), caterpillar-like larvae, phytophagous

animals.name: suborder: Apocrita
animals.traits:
hymenoptera: 2 pairs of membranous wings hooked together, reduced venation, chewing or lapping mouthparts
apocrita (wasps, bees, ants, parasitoid wasps): narrow wasp waist (petiole), ovipositor often turned into a sting, legless larvae
